turns.assessment: The hard, simultaneous loss is localized to the physical span adjacent to S14: OSC_LOS occurs on oms.S04-S14.span5 and on the corresponding reverse-direction oms.S14-S04.span0, with downstream amplifier and multi-channel OCH loss. Concurrent bidirectional OSC loss on the S14-S20 cable further supports excavation or duct damage affecting multiple cables. Stable amplifier pump telemetry argues strongly against an amplifier failure; a single channel, client, switch, or WSS fault cannot explain the all-channel optical and OSC losses.

proposals.rationale: E14 is the S04->S14 span immediately adjacent to S14 and raised OSC_LOS; its reverse physical counterpart E23 also lost OSC at exactly the same time. A cable cut normally severs both fibres and explains the bidirectional, all-channel loss affecting svc223. The simultaneous S14-S20 span alarms indicate a likely shared-duct excavation event.
A sufficiently severe bend, crushed cable, or damaged splice could lose both payload and OSC, but the abrupt bidirectional failure across multiple cables is more characteristic of a cut.
